commands.description:
Mark affiliate payouts paid

Record up to 20 due affiliate payouts as paid in one request, after you have paid the affiliates yourself. No money moves: SellApp only records the payment. Each payout marked paid also marks its referrals paid and emails that affiliate that the payout was paid. Send the payout IDs and `expected_total_usd_cents`, the sum of their `amount_usd_cents` as you read them, in integer USD cents (`4250` means $42.50). Every payout is checked first, and nothing changes when one of them is unknown in your store, is not `due`, or has referrals that no longer add up to it or can no longer be paid (`422` on `payout_ids`, one message per payout), or when the amounts add up to another total (`422` on `expected_total_usd_cents`). Then each payout is marked in the order sent, and `data` reports one `outcome` per payout: `paid`, `skipped`, or `failed`. A payout that changes between the check and its turn is skipped or fails without affecting the others. Requires the `affiliate` and `affiliate:payout` API-key abilities, and the staff member who owns the key needs the affiliate and affiliate payout permissions. There is no idempotency key, but sending the same batch again is refused with `422` on `payout_ids`, because those payouts are no longer due, so nobody is emailed twice. After a lost response, list the payouts with `GET /v2/affiliate-payouts?status=due` and send only those still due, with their new total. The emails cannot be taken back; to reopen a payout recorded by mistake, set it back to `due` with `PATCH /v2/affiliate-payouts/{payout}/status`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: expected_total_usd_cents
bodyFields.description: The sum of the payouts' `amount_usd_cents`, in integer USD cents, as you read them. If they add up to anything else, nothing is marked.

Resend an affiliate invitation

Email a pending affiliate invitation again, with a new sign-in link that expires after 6 hours, to the address it was created for. The invitation itself does not change: `invited_at` keeps the original date. Send no body. Requires the `affiliate` API-key ability, and the staff member who owns the key needs the affiliate and `store` permissions, the same as inviting an affiliate. Every refusal returns `422` on `invitation` and sends nothing: the invitation was already answered or is no longer pending, the affiliate program is not configured or turned off, the same invitation was sent within the last minute, your store reached its limit of 10 invitation emails per hour (new invitations and resends count together; the message says how many seconds to wait), or the email could not be sent. commands.description:
Save an affiliate coupon

Create the affiliate's coupon, or change it, in one call. When the affiliate has no coupon, send `code`, `type`, `discount`, and `store_wide`; each one you leave out returns `422` on that field. When a coupon exists, send only the fields to change; the others stay as they are. Any request also enables a coupon that was disabled, so `{}` re-enables it unchanged. A store-wide coupon returns `products: []`, and you can send a read coupon back unchanged. Coupon rules apply as for `PATCH /v2/coupons/{coupon}`: the code must be free in your store, `products` and `product_variants` must be yours, `expires_at` must be in the future, and a percentage `discount` cannot exceed 100; each refusal is keyed by that field. Amounts are decimals in the store currency's major unit. Re-enabling a disabled coupon emails the affiliate, when their membership is active, that their coupon is enabled again; creating or changing a coupon sends no email. Requires the `affiliate`, `affiliate:write`, and `coupon` API-key abilities, and the staff member who owns the key needs the affiliate, coupon, and `store` permissions. Safe to repeat: after a lost response, the same request leaves the same coupon, sends no second email, and never creates a second coupon. An affiliate of another store returns `404`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

commands.description:
Update affiliate products

Give one affiliate custom commission rates on chosen product variants, change those rates, or switch back to the program's rates. Send at least one of `enable_specific_products`, `products`, or `replace_products`; a field you leave out keeps what the affiliate has. With custom rates on, each entry in `products` sets the rate for one variant (`enabled: true` with a `commission`) or removes the variant (`enabled: false`); variants you do not name keep their rates. Add `replace_products: true` to make `products` the complete list instead. Turning custom rates on without `replace_products` keeps the program's current rate on every variant you do not name. `enable_specific_products: false` removes every custom rate, so the program's rates apply again; sending `products` with it returns `422`. Turning custom rates on for an affiliate who did not have them emails the affiliate that they have custom rates and emails your store a confirmation; other changes send nothing. Requires the `affiliate` and `affiliate:write` API-key abilities, and the staff member who owns the key needs both the affiliate and the `store` permission. Safe to repeat: the same request leaves the same rates and does not email again. Errors are keyed `products` (a variant that is not a published variant of your store, a repeated variant, or rates while custom rates stay off), `products.{i}.id`, `products.{i}.commission` (missing for an enabled variant), and `products.{i}.commission.type`, `products.{i}.commission.percentage` (0.01 to 100), or `products.{i}.commission.amount_usd_cents` (at least 1). commands.description:
Create a booking product

Create a draft booking product with one draft option that customers book as a timed appointment, one per purchase and one customer per time slot. Nothing can be booked until you publish it, whatever `visibility` you send: `visibility`, `PRIVATE` by default, applies once the product is published. Publish it with `POST /v2/products/{product}/publish`. Schedule fields you leave out take their defaults; read the result with `GET /v2/products/{product}/variants/{variant}/booking`. Each successful call creates another product, so do not retry blindly after a lost response: list your products first. Requires the `listing` API-key ability and the `listing` permission in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

sellapp bookings create --body '{"title":"Strategy consultation","description":"

A private strategy session for your next launch.

","variant_title":"60 minute session","price_cents":2500,"currency":"USD","payment_methods":["STRIPE"],"timezone":"Europe/London","duration_minutes":60,"availability":[{"day":1,"enabled":true,"start":"09:00","end":"12:00"},{"day":3,"enabled":true,"start":"13:00","end":"17:00"}]}' --yes

commands.description:
Create a charge

Create a standalone charge for payment or a free claim. Requires the charge API-key ability and store permission. The total is an integer in the currency's minor units: 1999 USD means $19.99. Supplying currency requires total. For a positive paid charge, choose enabled payment_method/payment_methods or use_all_payment_methods; availability depends on the store and currency. CUSTOM_PAYMENT_METHOD is supported: preselection requires custom_payment_method_id. custom_payment_method_ids optionally restricts the available custom methods; omission snapshots the currently usable IDs for this store, without product assignments. Customer proof or confirmation changes custom charges to REVIEW, not COMPLETED. Creating a charge does not prove payment. A repeated create may create another charge; check the original result before retrying. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.
commands.example: sellapp charges create --email 'sofia.rivera@example.com' --return-url https://example.com/launch-complete --currency USD --total 10000 --payment-method PAYPAL --reference 'One more thing launch' --yes

bodyFields.description: Supported three-letter currency code, normalized to uppercase. Defaults to USD when omitted. When supplied, total is required; supply both for a paid charge.

bodyFields.name: total
bodyFields.description: Integer minor units in currency; 1999 USD is $19.99. Required when currency is supplied. Maximum is the minor-unit equivalent of 99,999,999 major currency units. Omit total and currency together for a free USD claim.

commands.description:
Retrieve the charge summary

Total your store's completed charges for a date range and compare them with the period of the same length just before it, as the charges analytics page does. Only `COMPLETED` charges count, dated by when they completed; pending, voided, and failed charges are left out. `revenue` is in integer minor units of the store currency, converted from each charge's USD total: `12450` means $124.50 in USD. Send `start_date` and `end_date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` days in the store's time zone, both included, or a `preset`; dates take precedence over `preset`, and without either the summary covers `last_30_days`. An unknown `preset` or a date not in `YYYY-MM-DD` form returns `422` on that parameter, and a range that ends before it starts returns `422` on `start_date` when you sent `start_date`, otherwise `end_date`. Requires the `charge` API-key ability and the charge permission in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: A named range in the store's time zone: `today`, `yesterday`, `this_week`, `last_week`, `this_month`, `last_month`, `last_7_days`, `last_30_days` (the default), or `all_time`. `this_week`, `this_month`, and the `last_*_days` presets end today. `all_time` starts on the day the store was created or took its first order, whichever is earlier. Ignored when `start_date` or `end_date` is sent.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: First day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the store's time zone. Inclusive. Sent without `end_date`, the range runs to the end of today.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the store's time zone. Inclusive. Sent without `start_date`, the range starts on the day the store was created or took its first order, whichever is earlier.

List why community access grants failed across all platforms, with how many grants failed for each reason and what you can do about it, most frequent first. A grant is the access a purchase gives a customer, such as a Discord role or a place in a Telegram group. Only reasons that still need attention or are retried are counted; failures nobody can act on, such as a customer who left the server, are not. Only SellApp's records are read; no platform is contacted. An empty `data` array means no grant is failing. Requires the `community` API-key ability and the `community` permission in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

commands.description:
Remove a community server

Remove one Discord server, Slack channel, Telegram group or channel, or WhatsApp group from the store, and clear it from every product variant that gives access through it, including deleted ones. Buyers of those variants get no access through it from then on. SellApp does not contact the platform: members, roles and the bot stay as they are there. Removing the last Telegram or WhatsApp group also disconnects that platform. Confirm the variants first: read them with `GET` on the same path and send their IDs as `affected_variant_ids` (in any order). When they differ from the variants that use it now, the request returns `422` on `affected_variant_ids` and nothing is removed. Leave `affected_variant_ids` out, or send an empty list, when no variant uses it. Clients that cannot send a body with `DELETE` can send the IDs in the query string instead, as `affected_variant_ids[]=902`. A repeated request returns `404` once it is removed. Requires the `community` API-key ability and both the `store` and `community` permissions in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.
commands.example: sellapp community-connections servers remove --platform discord server_ship_room --body '{"affected_variant_ids":[902]}' --yes

commands.description:
Start a community connection

Start the provider-specific connection flow. OAuth providers return a connect URL containing encrypted state bound to the authenticated actor, store, platform, and purpose; that state expires after 15 minutes and securely authorizes the provider callback without forwarding the API bearer token or requiring a SellApp dashboard session. Open the URL exactly as issued, then poll the connection list with the original bearer token after the provider redirects. Do not append credentials, reconstruct, or reuse the URL. Legacy unsigned Slack URLs are rejected, so clients must call this endpoint again to restart those flows. Telegram returns a short-lived verification token, and WhatsApp returns a pollable QR session. The provider application must be configured, and Discord server connections require a connected Discord account. Requires the `community` Sanctum ability. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

commands.description:
Create a coupon

Create a discount code for your store.

bodyFields.name: discount
bodyFields.description: A decimal discount value of at least 1. Percentage discounts cannot exceed 100; amount discounts use the store currency's major unit. A `subscriptions` coupon cannot take 100% off: that returns `422` on `discount`, so offer a free trial instead.

bodyFields.name: products
bodyFields.description: Product IDs the coupon applies to when store_wide is false. Each product you add must sell a variant of the coupon's kind: a subscription plan for a `subscriptions` coupon, or a one-time variant for a `one_time` one. Another product returns `422` on `products`.

bodyFields.name: product_variants
bodyFields.description: Optional variant restrictions. Every variant must belong to a selected product. Products without listed variants remain eligible on all variants. Each variant you add must be of the coupon's kind, a subscription plan or a one-time variant; another returns `422` on `product_variants`.

bodyFields.name: expires_at
bodyFields.description: A future date and time, or null for no expiry.

bodyFields.name: minimum_amount
bodyFields.description: A decimal minimum amount in the store currency's major unit that the order lines of the coupon's kind must reach, or null for no minimum.

bodyFields.name: applies_to
bodyFields.description: What the coupon discounts: `one_time` for one-time purchases, or `subscriptions` for the first payments of a subscription plan. A new coupon defaults to `one_time`, and an update that leaves this out keeps the current kind. The coupon only discounts order lines of its kind.

bodyFields.name: subscription_payments
bodyFields.description: How many payments a `subscriptions` coupon discounts, counting the signup payment as the first, so `3` discounts the signup and the next two renewals. A `subscriptions` coupon needs one, and an update that leaves it out keeps the stored number. Missing on a `subscriptions` coupon, or outside 1 to 36, it returns `422` on `subscription_payments` with `The number of discounted payments must be between 1 and 36.` A `one_time` coupon always stores null here.

commands.description:
Create an invoice

Create an invoice for one or more product variants. Credit products are direct-only: send a credits variant by itself, use a quantity covered by its credit rate tiers, and respect the variant quantity increment rules. A subscription plan that offers a trial is priced at the trial, nothing for a free trial and the trial price for a paid one, unless the customer already had a trial of that product; then it is priced at the plan price. Two requests racing for the same trial can be refused with a `422` on `invoice`. A cart carries at most one subscription plan and nothing else; a plan mixed with other products or with a second plan returns `422` on `product_variants.{variant_id}`, and a plan's `quantity` other than 1 returns `422` on `quantity`. A customer who already holds the plan, matched by `customer_email`, is refused with `422` on `invoice` while that subscription is active, trialing, past due, or unpaid, whichever payment method bills it. A subscription scheduled to end still blocks while it can be kept, and the message then tells the customer to keep it from the customer portal. One that can no longer be kept, such as a PayPal subscription cancelled at period end, does not block. For an in-house subscription on hold for an unpaid renewal, the message tells the customer to pay and resume it from the customer portal. A `coupon` discounts only the lines of its kind, set by the coupon's `applies_to`. A `subscriptions` coupon discounts the plan's first `subscription_payments` payments when the `payment_method` can carry the discount: Stripe, which carries more than one discounted payment only on a monthly or yearly plan, or a method the store bills in house. On PayPal, Razorpay, or a weekly or daily Stripe plan discounted for more than one payment, the plan sells at its full price and the coupon is left off the order without an error. A coupon for the other kind, a `subscriptions` coupon on a plan that starts with a trial, and a fixed amount that would make the plan free each return `422` on `coupon`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.description: The IP address the customer is buying from. Send it when you sell a plan with a trial: a trial of the same product taken from this address in the last 30 days counts as the customer's. Without it, only `customer_email` is checked, so a customer could take another trial with a new email address.

commands.description:
Create invoice refund

Request a full or partial provider refund using the same idempotent refund ledger as the dashboard. This sends real money back to the customer. Amounts are decimal currency strings, never floating-point numbers. Send the invoice's `payment.refunded_total_cents` unchanged as `expected_refunded_total_cents` so that a repeated or concurrent request is refused instead of refunding twice: the refund goes out only while the refunded total is still the amount you sent. A changed total returns `422` on `expected_refunded_total_cents`; read the invoice again before deciding whether to refund. Other refusals return `422` on `refund`, including, when you send `expected_refunded_total_cents`, a refund still pending on the order. Requires the `invoice` token ability. bodyFields.description: The refunded total you expect, in integer minor units of the invoice's `payment.refund_currency`, which can differ from the invoice currency: `500` means $5.00 in USD. Read it from `payment.refunded_total_cents` on the invoice and send it unchanged; it is `0` before the first refund. After a refund, `data.invoice.payment.refunded_total_cents` in the response is the value to send with the next one. With this field, the refund goes out only while the refunded total still equals it and no other refund on the order is pending. Omit it or send null to refund without the check.

commands.description:
Create an order

Create an order with one or more product-variant line items and start checkout. This can create provider payment sessions, reserve stock or wallet funds, and begin fulfillment for a free or fully wallet-funded order. Requires the invoice ability or orders:write OAuth scope and current store permission. Use the same Idempotency-Key and identical body after a lost response; inspect the order before creating a new key. The payment.checkout_url is a handoff, not proof of payment. A subscription plan that offers a trial is priced at the trial, nothing for a free trial and the trial price for a paid one, unless the customer already had a trial of that product, matched by `customer_email` or a recent `customer_ip`; then it is priced at the plan price. Two requests racing for the same trial can be refused with a `422` on `invoice`. A cart carries at most one subscription plan and nothing else; a plan mixed with other products or with a second plan returns `422` on `product_variants.{variant_id}`, and a plan's `quantity` other than 1 returns `422` on `quantity`. A customer who already holds the plan, matched by `customer_email`, is refused with `422` on `invoice` while that subscription is active, trialing, past due, or unpaid, whichever payment method bills it. A subscription scheduled to end still blocks while it can be kept, and the message then tells the customer to keep it from the customer portal. One that can no longer be kept, such as a PayPal subscription cancelled at period end, does not block. For an in-house subscription on hold for an unpaid renewal, the message tells the customer to pay and resume it from the customer portal. A `coupon` discounts only the lines of its kind, set by the coupon's `applies_to`. A `subscriptions` coupon discounts the plan's first `subscription_payments` payments when the `payment_method` can carry the discount: Stripe, which carries more than one discounted payment only on a monthly or yearly plan, or a method the store bills in house. On PayPal, Razorpay, or a weekly or daily Stripe plan discounted for more than one payment, the plan sells at its full price and the coupon is left off the order without an error. A coupon for the other kind, a `subscriptions` coupon on a plan that starts with a trial, and a fixed amount that would make the plan free each return `422` on `coupon`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: customer_ip
bodyFields.description: The IP address the customer is buying from. Send it when you sell a plan with a trial: a trial of the same product taken from this address in the last 30 days counts as the customer's. Without it, only `customer_email` is checked, so a customer could take another trial with a new email address.

bodyFields.name: custom_payment_method_id
bodyFields.description: Required when payment_method is CUSTOM_PAYMENT_METHOD. ULID of an enabled custom payment method belonging to this store.

commands.description:
Create order checkout

Start or reuse checkout for a PENDING order. A new payment session returns 201; if the order already has one, that session is returned with 200. An order that costs nothing, or that the customer wallet covers in full, is marked as paid and returns 200 with a null payment.checkout_url. A free trial sold through Stripe, PayPal, or Razorpay is the exception: the customer still has to authorise the subscription with that provider, so checkout returns its payment.checkout_url and the order stays PENDING until they do. An unpaid order that sold a trial stops being payable after 72 hours, or on those three providers once the trial it sold is about to end; checkout then returns 422 on order.checkout, the order stays PENDING, and the customer has to start a new checkout. An order that is no longer PENDING also returns 422 on order.checkout. Other failures can mark the order FAILED and release wallet reservations. Do not infer payment from a checkout URL or browser return. The optional expected_status field is validated but is not a checkout concurrency precondition. Requires the `invoice` API-key ability or the `orders:write` OAuth scope, and current store permission. `Idempotency-Key` is required. Reuse the same key and identical request after a lost response; changed input or an in-progress request returns `409`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: expected_status
bodyFields.description: Validated status value; checkout does not compare it with current status. Retrieve the order before retrying.

commands.description:
Create and pay an order from a wallet

Create an order and debit the customer's wallet in one atomic call. This spends real wallet funds and queues normal fulfillment; PAID means payment was captured, while COMPLETED depends on fulfillment. Requires both invoice and wallet:write API-key abilities and both store permissions. Wallets must be enabled, the customer must already exist in this store, and an active wallet must cover the entire positive total after discounts and taxes. Subscriptions and partial wallet payments are not supported. Omit payment_method and custom_payment_method_id. An insufficient balance or invalid cart returns 422 without creating an order or debit. Send the required Idempotency-Key; retry an identical request with the same key after a lost response. Reusing it with different input returns 409. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: customer_ip
bodyFields.description: The IP address the customer is buying from. Send it when you sell a plan with a trial: a trial of the same product taken from this address in the last 30 days counts as the customer's. Without it, only `customer_email` is checked, so a customer could take another trial with a new email address.

commands.description:
Refund an order

Request a real refund for a completed, nonsubscription order with refundable balance and a supported provider. amount is a decimal string in the order's `totals.refund_currency`: "5.00" means $5.00 in USD, not 500 cents. Omitting amount, sending null, or an empty string requests the FULL remaining balance. Do not send amount_cents: it is not a request field. Inspect refund.status (pending/effective/failed/cancelled); a 200 response does not guarantee money has reached the customer. Retrieve refund state before retrying an uncertain provider outcome. Send the order's `totals.refunded_total_cents` unchanged as `expected_refunded_total_cents` so that a retry under a new Idempotency-Key, or a refund someone else made meanwhile, is refused instead of refunding twice: the refund goes out only while the order's refunded total still equals it. A changed total returns `422` on `expected_refunded_total_cents`; read the order again before deciding whether to refund. An invalid `amount` returns `422` on `amount`; other refusals return `422` on `refund`, including, when you send `expected_refunded_total_cents`, a refund still pending on the order. Requires the `invoice` API-key ability or the `orders:write` OAuth scope, and current store permission. `Idempotency-Key` is required. Reuse the same key and identical request after a lost response; changed input or an in-progress request returns `409`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: amount
bodyFields.description: Decimal major-unit amount in the order's `totals.refund_currency`, positive and no greater than remaining balance. Precision follows that currency. Omission/null/empty requests the full remaining balance.

bodyFields.name: expected_refunded_total_cents
bodyFields.description: The refunded total you expect, in integer minor units of the order's `totals.refund_currency`, which can differ from the order currency: `500` means $5.00 in USD. Read it from `totals.refunded_total_cents` on the order and send it unchanged; it is `0` before the first refund. After a refund, `data.order.totals.refunded_total_cents` in the response is the value to send with the next one. With this field, the refund goes out only while the refunded total still equals it and no other refund on the order is pending. Omit it or send null to refund without the check.

commands.description:

commands.description:
Update a payment method modifier

Set the discount or fee customers get at checkout when they pay with this payment method. Send `kind` with positive amounts: `fee` adds them to the price and `discount` takes them off. A discount or fee needs `percentage`, `fixed_amount` or both; send `kind: none` with both `null` to remove it. Both amount fields are required and may be `null`, and the amounts you send replace the current ones. The condition works differently: leave out both `condition` and `threshold` to keep the condition the method has now, even one changed in the dashboard while your request was in flight; send `condition: null` to remove it so every checkout gets the discount or fee; send `condition` with `threshold` to set it. A percentage over 100 returns `422` on `percentage`, and a fixed amount over 100000 returns `422` on `fixed_amount`. Sending the modifier the method already has returns `200` and changes nothing, so a retry is safe; the `data` of `GET /v2/payment-methods/{paymentMethod}/modifier` without `payment_method` is such a request. commands.description:
Duplicate a product

Copy a normal product, bundle, add-on, credits product, or booking product within the same store and return the copy. Courses cannot be duplicated. The copy is titled `(Copy)`, `(Copy 2)`, and so on, with a matching `-copy` slug, and keeps every other product setting, including its images, `visibility`, and draft state. A copy of a published product is therefore on sale straight away. It gets no place in the product order or in a section. A normal product's variants are copied with their settings and downloadable files, except subscription variants. A bundle's variant is copied with the products in it, an add-on's with its downloadable files and the products it is offered with, a credits product's with its rate tiers, and a booking product's options, except subscription options, with their schedules. Never copied: sales, reviews, appointments, serial codes, issued licence keys, and group membership. A copied variant that delivers serial codes gets a stock of `0`, so it shows as sold out until you add codes. Requires the `listing` API-key ability and the `listing` permission in your team role. Not safe to retry blindly: every call creates another copy. If a response is lost, list your products and look for the copy before trying again. A course, or a product with nothing to copy (only subscription variants), returns `422` on `product`. A product that changed while the copy was being made also returns `422` on `product`; nothing was copied. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

commands.description:
Publish a product

Publish a draft product so customers can buy it. Works for normal products, bundles, add-ons, credits products, booking products, and courses. Each is checked as saved, the way its dashboard editor checks it before publishing, and nothing else about the product changes. A normal product needs a description and at least one published variant, and every variant that will be on sale needs a title, a description of at least 5 characters, a working delivery (for example an uploaded file for a download), a price, and payment methods enabled for the store that can take that currency. With exactly one variant, that variant is published with the product. With several, send the draft variants to publish with it in `variant_ids`; the others stay drafts. Publishing a subscription variant also creates its billing plans with the payment providers. A booking product publishes its one option with it; with several options, publish at least one with `POST /v2/products/{product}/variants/{variant}/publish` first, and the other options keep their own state. A bundle needs at least one product in it. A course is published with `visibility`, or with its saved visibility when you leave it out; `PUBLIC` also needs a ready promo video and at least one published lesson. A subscription-priced course cannot be published here. Publishing does not change a normal product's `visibility`: a product that is not `PUBLIC` is published but stays off the storefront listing. Requires the `listing` API-key ability and the `listing` permission in your team role. Safe to repeat: once the product is published, another call changes nothing and returns `422` with `The product is already published.` on `product`. Every refusal returns `422`. `visibility` is accepted only for a course and `variant_ids` only for a normal product; each is otherwise refused on that field, and `variant_ids.{i}` names an ID that is not a variant of this product. Everything else is on `product`, with one sentence per thing the product still needs. One `product` refusal comes after the product was published: when a payment provider refuses to create a subscription billing plan, the product and its variants are already published and the message is the provider's reason. Retrieve the product before trying again. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: variant_ids
bodyFields.description: Normal products only. IDs of this product's draft variants to publish with it. Needed when the product has several variants and none is published yet; a single variant is published anyway. Draft variants you leave out stay drafts.

Create a promotion

Create a promotion and its initial ordered phase set. `applies_to` chooses whether it discounts one-time purchases or the first `subscription_payments` payments of a subscription plan, and a subscription promotion can be limited to picked products and plans with `store_wide`, `products`, and `product_variants`. bodyFields.description: What the promotion discounts: `one_time` for one-time purchases, or `subscriptions` for the first payments of a subscription plan. A new promotion defaults to `one_time`, and an update that leaves this out keeps the current kind. The promotion only discounts order lines of its kind.

bodyFields.name: subscription_payments
bodyFields.description: How many payments a `subscriptions` promotion discounts, counting the signup payment as the first, so `3` discounts the signup and the next two renewals. A `subscriptions` promotion needs one, and an update that leaves it out keeps the stored number. Missing on a `subscriptions` promotion, or outside 1 to 36, it returns `422` on `subscription_payments` with `The number of discounted payments must be between 1 and 36.` A `one_time` promotion always stores null here.

A new promotion defaults to `true`, an update that leaves it out keeps the current scope, and switching a promotion to `one_time` makes it store-wide again. A `one_time` promotion with `false` returns `422` on `store_wide` with `A promotion for one-time purchases applies to the whole store.`

Each one must sell a subscription, or the request returns `422` on `products` with `Pick only products that sell a subscription.` A narrowed promotion left with no products returns `422` with `Pick at least one subscription product for this promotion.` An update replaces the picks with this list, or keeps them when it is left out.

Each one must be a subscription plan of a product in `products`, or the request returns `422` on `product_variants` with `Pick only subscription plans of the picked products.` A picked product with none of its plans listed takes every plan, including plans added later. commands.description:
Send a sender email verification

Ask SellApp's email provider, Amazon SES, to email a verification link to the address: the first step of using your own address as the sender of customer emails. The store's sender does not change yet, so `email` stays `null` and customer emails keep coming from `default_from`. The address must be valid and its domain must accept email, and no other store may use it as its sender. The store must not have a sender email already: remove it first with `DELETE /v2/store/settings/sender-email`. Limits: one verification email per address and five per store in 24 hours; a refused request returns `422` on `email` with when the next one can be sent, and does not count. `422` on `email` too when another store is setting up the address. `503` when the email provider does not accept the request: nothing changed, try again later. Do not repeat a successful request: open the link in the email already sent. The example omits `email`, which is always `null` in this response. Requires the `store` API-key ability and the `store` permission in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.description: The address customer emails should come from.

commands.description:
Set the sender email

Make a verified address the store's sender: customer emails then come from it, with the sender name from the personalization settings. Send the address you sent a verification email to with `POST /v2/store/settings/sender-email/verification` after its owner opened the link. Refused with `422` on `email` when the link was not opened yet, when this store did not send the address a verification email in the last 7 days, or when the store already has another sender (remove it first). Sending the current sender again returns `200` with the current state and changes nothing, so a retry is safe. Requires the `store` API-key ability and the `store` permission in your team role. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: shopping_cart_enabled
bodyFields.description: Whether customers can add several products to a cart and buy them in one checkout. `false` turns the storefront cart off.

bodyFields.name: customer_email_required
bodyFields.description: Whether checkout asks customers for an email address. With `false`, checkout does not ask, and delivery and payment emails cannot reach a customer who left none.

bodyFields.name: allow_vpn_purchases
bodyFields.description: Whether customers who use a VPN or a proxy can buy.

bodyFields.name: blacklist_on_dispute
bodyFields.description: Whether a customer's email address and IP address are added to your blacklist when they open a payment dispute.

bodyFields.name: minimum_spend
bodyFields.description: The smallest order total, VAT included, that customers can check out with, as a decimal string in the order's currency: `"12.50"` on a USD order means $12.50. At least `1`; digits with an optional decimal part, no sign or exponent. Send `null` or `"0"` to remove the minimum; it then reads `null`.

bodyFields.name: billing_descriptor
bodyFields.description: The purchase name customers see while they check out, up to 20 characters. `null` uses the default, `SellApp Order`.

bodyFields.name: attempts_per_customer
bodyFields.description: How many checkout attempts one customer can make within the window, counted per IP address and email pair, or per checkout session fingerprint when checkout does not ask for an email. 1 to 100000; the default is `5`. This limit cannot be removed.

bodyFields.name: attempts_per_ip
bodyFields.description: How many checkout attempts can come from one IP address within the window. 1 to 100000; `null` turns this limit off.

bodyFields.name: attempts_per_email
bodyFields.description: How many checkout attempts can use one customer email address within the window. 1 to 100000; `null` turns this limit off.

bodyFields.name: attempts_per_fingerprint
bodyFields.description: How many checkout attempts can come from one checkout session fingerprint (a browser identifier) within the window. 1 to 100000; `null` turns this limit off.

bodyFields.name: rate_limit_window_seconds
bodyFields.description: How long each checkout limit counts attempts before allowing them again, in seconds: 60 (one minute) to 604800 (seven days). The default is `3600` (one hour). Attempts are counted per store.

commands.description:
Update crypto checkout settings

Replace both crypto checkout values, for a store that takes crypto through SellApp's crypto processor; `underpaid_percentage` and `minimum_confirmations` are required. SellApp sends the changed values to the crypto processor and saves them only once it accepts them; an unchanged value is not sent. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

bodyFields.name: underpaid_percentage
bodyFields.description: How far short of the amount due, in percent, a crypto payment can be and still count as paid: `2` accepts a payment up to 2% short. 0 to 100.

bodyFields.name: minimum_confirmations
bodyFields.description: How many blockchain confirmations a crypto payment needs before the order is processed. 1 to 25.

commands.description:
Create a store

Create a store owned by the authenticated user, with the same defaults as dashboard creation. Requires stores:create on an unrestricted user-owned API key, or the official CLI OAuth admin grant. Customer and browser sessions and direct MCP bearer tokens are rejected; MCP uses reviewed server delegation. Selected-store keys cannot create stores. No existing store or X-STORE header is needed; Name and slug are required; slug is normalized to lowercase. Visibility defaults to PUBLIC. This does not change your dashboard's selected store. Idempotency-Key is required and retained for 24 hours: reuse the same key and identical body after a lost response. A conflicting request returns 409; invalid or duplicate slugs return 422. Retries are bound to the user and operation across token rotation and supported credential types; current authorization is checked before replay. Store defaults and the successful retry receipt commit together. You can create one new store per user every 60 seconds, across all credentials. A new creation during that interval returns 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers. Wait for that delay and retry the same key and body. Replaying a successful original key recovers its store without creating another or consuming another creation allowance.

bodyFields.name: slug
bodyFields.description: Lowercased before validation. Reserved infrastructure names such as api, www and cdn are unavailable.

commands.description:
Dismiss a subscription action

Dismiss a pending lifecycle action that the provider left unresolved, which frees the subscription for its next change. Only a pending action can be dismissed, and the required `note` is stored on the action as its `error` so the decision stays on the record. An action in any other state returns `422` with the refusal sentence under `errors.subscription`, while a missing or over-long `note` returns an ordinary field error. This operation does not replay completed dismissals: idempotency keys are ignored. After a lost response, retrieve the action before repeating the request; an already-dismissed action returns `422`. Requires the `invoice` Sanctum ability. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.
commands.example: sellapp subscriptions actions dismiss --product-subscription 124 4207 --note 'Confirmed with the customer that they no longer want the upgrade.' --yes

bodyFields.name: idempotency_key

commands.description:
Create a support automation rule

Create an automation rule, paused unless you send `is_active: true`. Once switched on, a rule answers new matching tickets without anyone on your team: it posts its template as a reply to the customer, can credit a refund to the customer's store wallet, and can close the ticket. Create it paused, test it with the dry run, then switch it on with the state endpoint. `name` and `response_template_id` are required. Conditions you leave out or send as `null` match every ticket. Amounts are integer USD cents (`1999` means $19.99), and `action_refund_percent_basis` is in hundredths of a percent (`5000` is 50%). A field the rule does not take returns `422` naming it. The new rule is checked after your existing rules. Requires the `support.automation` API-key ability, and the key's user needs the Support Automation role in the store (owners and administrators have it). Not safe to retry blindly: a repeated request creates a second rule, so list the rules first when a response is lost. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

Send both or neither; `null` on both answers any reason. A store reason must be active and offered for every product. Read the codes from the support reason options endpoint.

bodyFields.name: match_product_ids

At most 200 distinct IDs of your store's products; a repeated, unknown or deleted product returns `422` on `match_product_ids.{index}`, except a product the rule already names.

commands.description:
Dry run support automation rules

See what your automation would do with one of your tickets if it were opened now: which rule would answer it, the reply it would send, the refund in USD cents and the close outcome. Nothing is sent, refunded, closed or recorded. Only switched-on rules take part, in their current order, so a paused rule shows up only after you switch it on. With support automation off, the answer is `matched: false` with `skip_reason: auto_respond_disabled`. Update a support automation rule state

Switch a rule on (`active`) or off (`paused`), archives it (`archived`), or brings an archived rule back (`restored`) in the on or off state it had. Render a support reply template

Fill a reply template for one of your tickets and get the text back, ready for you to send as a reply. Nothing is sent, saved or refunded. The ticket supplies the customer's email, the ticket and order numbers, the product title, the store name, the customer's wallet balance, and its latest wallet refund that is still standing as `refund_amount`. Requires the `ticket` API-key ability, and the key's user must be allowed to manage tickets in the store (the Resolution Center role, or owner or administrator). Safe to retry. commands.description:
Refund a ticket to the customer's wallet

Credit the customer's store wallet for one item of the ticket's order and send `customer_note` to the customer. This moves money: the credit is store credit in USD that the customer can spend in your store, and the note is posted as your reply on the ticket, which emails it to the customer. The ticket stays open. Read the ticket's wallet refund options first, then send the item's `invoice_id`, the `amount_cents` to credit (at most its `refundable_cents`) and `expected_refundable_cents` equal to the `refundable_cents` you read. If what is left to refund changed since you read it, the request returns `422` on `expected_refundable_cents` and credits nothing: read the options again. Amounts are integer USD cents: `500` means $5.00. Requires both the `ticket` and `support.refund` API-key abilities, and the store member needs both the ticket and the support refund permissions. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header; requests without one return `400`. Retrying with the same key and identical body within 24 hours returns the original refund with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does not credit or email the customer again. Never retry under a new key: the first refund already lowered what is left, so the retry returns `422` on `expected_refundable_cents`, and a request with the same amount and note as an earlier refund of this item returns `422` on `customer_note`. Change the note if you mean to credit the customer a second time. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.
commands.example: sellapp tickets wallet-refunds create 312 --invoice-id 5120 --amount-cents 500 --expected-refundable-cents 1999 --customer-note 'We added $5.00 to your store wallet for the trouble with your download link.' --yes

bodyFields.name: expected_refundable_cents

bodyFields.description: Message to the customer, at least 6 characters after trimming. It is posted on the ticket and emailed. A leftover placeholder such as `{refund_amount}` is refused.

commands.description:
Reverse a ticket's wallet refund

Take a wallet refund issued from this ticket back out of the customer's wallet, and return the refund with `reversed` `true` and its `reversal`. commands.description:
Notify variant buyers

Email your customers that this variant has new content: every completed order that delivered its downloadable files gets one email. The emails are queued, so `202` means they were queued, not delivered. It sends only for a published variant with at least one file, at least one such order, and no upload in progress. The buyers of one variant can be emailed this way at most once an hour, whichever API key or team member sends it, and each team member can send at most 3 times a minute per variant. Requires the `listing` API-key ability and the `listing` permission in your team role. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header; requests without one return `400`. A retry with the same key and an empty body returns the first response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and sends nothing new. Use a new key for every send you intend, including a new attempt after a `422`. The same key while the first request is still running returns `409`. Every refusal is `422` on `variant`: a draft variant, a variant without files, a variant nobody has bought, an upload still in progress, the hourly limit (the message says how many minutes are left), the per-minute limit, or another send for the same variant at the same moment. Check `GET` on the same path first to see the numbers. A variant of another product returns `404`. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.

commands.description:
Adjust a customer wallet

Add money to or take money from a customer's wallet and save the change as a `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` entry with your note. Amounts are integer USD cents: `2500` adds $25.00 and `-2500` takes $25.00 away. A first write returns `201`. The customer is not emailed. Adding money opens a wallet for a customer who has none yet. When the store's wallet settings have `expiration_days`, money you add expires after that many days, shown in the entry's `expires_at`. Requires the `wallet:write` API-key ability and the wallet permission in your team role. Send `expected_balance_cents` with the balance you last read to apply the change only while the wallet still holds exactly that balance. If the balance changed, the request returns `422` on `expected_balance_cents` and nothing is written; read the wallet again before deciding. A customer without a wallet counts as a balance of `0`. For safe retries, `idempotency_key` identifies one adjustment. Repeating the same key with the same customer, amount, and note (compared without leading and trailing spaces), made by the same staff member, returns `200` with the original entry and writes nothing, even when the balance has moved on since (the expected balance is not compared again). The same key with a different amount, note, or customer returns `422` on `wallet` and changes nothing. Keys are unique across all stores, are kept permanently, and cannot start with a reserved internal prefix such as `cashback:` or `topup_bonus:` (`422` on `idempotency_key`), so use a random value such as a UUID. Other refusals return `422` on `wallet` without writing: wallets are turned off for the store, the wallet is frozen, a debit is larger than the balance left after checkout holds, or a debit targets a customer who has no wallet yet. commands.description:
Reverse a wallet transaction

Undo one top-up or manual adjustment in a customer's wallet. SellApp writes a `REVERSAL` entry for the opposite amount, in integer USD cents, and returns it with `201`. Reversing a `TOP_UP` also reverses its `TOP_UP_BONUS`, so the balance drops by the top-up plus its bonus; the returned entry reverses the top-up itself. Reversing a negative `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` gives the money back, except credit that the debit had spent and that has since been refunded: a clawback entry takes that part back. The customer is not emailed, and no payment is refunded: reversing a paid top-up does not return money to the customer's card. Requires the `wallet:write` API-key ability and the wallet permission in your team role. Only `TOP_UP` and `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` entries can be reversed, once each, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed. Every refusal returns `422` on `transaction` and writes nothing: the entry was already reversed, is a reversal, is an expired credit, or is a type only the system reverses (`TOP_UP_BONUS` goes with its top-up, `CASHBACK` and `REWARD` are reversed by the system, a `REFUND` on its support ticket, a `PURCHASE_DEBIT` through its order); wallets are turned off for the store; or the money is reserved by a checkout or already spent. A customer of another store, a customer without a wallet, or an entry from another customer's wallet returns `404`. Send `expected_balance_cents` with the balance you read to reverse only while the wallet still holds it; otherwise the request returns `422` on `expected_balance_cents` and nothing changes. Repeating the request never takes the money twice: without a key, the repeat returns `422` because the entry is already reversed. To get the original `201` response back instead, send an `Idempotency-Key` header and repeat the same key with the same body within 24 hours; the replay carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The same key with a different body returns `409`. To put money back after a reversal, make a new manual adjustment. OAuth callers use the admin grant and select a store with X-STORE. Current membership and role permissions apply to every request.
commands.example: sellapp wallet transactions reverse --customer 42 501 --note 'Credit went to the wrong customer' --expected-balance-cents 2500 --yes
